newsitem.title: GERMANY: German papers call France's Juppe vital sacrifice.
newsitem.headline: German papers call France's Juppe vital sacrifice.

text.p: German commentators on Tuesday said the resignation of French Prime Minister Alain Juppe was the first sacrifice of the country's parliamentary election, but it could still not be enough for victory for the centre-right.
"Whether this emergency sacrifice at the alter of the electorate will be enough is still very questionable," wrote the Neue Osnabruecker Zeitung daily in a commentary.

Bonn's General Anzeiger said President Jacques Chirac had been forced to sacrifice his loyal lieutenant Juppe in a last-ditch bid to save his centre-right coalition, outpolled by the left-wing opposition in the first round.

"An atmosphere of catastrophe rules in the Elysee. The neo-Gaullist head of state has done something which he wanted to avoid at all costs," it wrote. "The case is another example of the fact that Chirac is not a good election tactician."

Juppe has borne the brunt of blame for austerity, high taxes and record unemployment in the two years since Chirac took office and was widely held responsible for the conservatives' poor showing in Sunday's first round.
"Many French linked social dismantling and record unemployment of recent years with his name," wrote the Neues Deutschland daily.
The Frankfurter Rundschau said despite the good showing of the left-wing on Sunday, Socialist leader Lionel Jospin still had a battle ahead of him.

"To win the election they (the Socialists) still need a partner (the Communists) which as one of the few communist parties has not yet showed its democratic complexion and is openly hostile to Europe," it wrote.
"But the loser is already clear -- Jacques Chirac."
